claims.text: "The default's constant value as text, or None when it is not a literal."
claims.why: The function returns str(value) for ast.Constant or resolved Name, None otherwise (including when expr is None).

claims.text: "Syntactic evidence first, then the enclosing signature, then the name."
claims.why: Code first checks platform tokens, then secret tokens, then walks parents for syntactic patterns (int/float/bool/Path calls, comparisons, if/ifexp), then checks return annotation, then name tokens.

claims.text: "Does an unset variable still yield a usable value at this site? Evidence, in order: a DEFAULT-named constant in the same statement; the read sitting in a non-final ``or`` operand (something else answers when it is empty); a conditional expression; or -- when the read is stashed in a local -- a later statement in the same block that consumes that local through a DEFAULT constant, an ``if/else``, or a conditional expression."
claims.why: Code checks: stmt with DEFAULT constant (line 107-109), then parents for BoolOp Or with any operand except last (lines 110-113), then IfExp with node in test (lines 114-115), then for local variable (Assign to single Name) checks downstream siblings for IfExp or If with test mentioning local (lines 123-131). Order matches docstring.

claims.text: "The guard must be ABOUT this local. Any `or`/`if` anywhere in a long statement that merely happens to mention it is not evidence -- that loose form silently un-darkened three provider API keys."
claims.why: The code (lines 124-131) only considers IfExp and If nodes where the test mentions the local (via _mentions), not any subexpression that merely contains the name.

observations.what: _resolve_default returns empty string for None value (expr.value is None) after converting to str, consistent with docstring 'None when it is not a literal'? Actually it returns '' for None, not None, but docstring says returns None when not literal, not when value is None. The code returns '' for None value, which is not None. This is a minor inconsistency: the docstring says returns None when not a literal, but for ast.Constant with value None, it returns empty string, not None. However, the docstring also says 'constant value as text', so empty string is text. The claim about returning None is only for non-literal cases. So it's kept but note the edge case.
_classify_kind uses _tokens and _src which are not defined in this chunk, making some claims uncheckable.
_fallback_evidence uses _contains and _mentions which are not defined in this chunk, making downstream checks unverifiable.
